messages:
alex: Heads-up — seen a regression in host-side CPU during the 1000qps load test. p95 decode latency increased ~20% after the kernel-selector change.
jin: Yikes. I glanced at the trace, flamegraph shows chunky CPU in parse_stream::chunk_assembler and kv_cache::evict_if_needed.
maria: When did the selector change roll? Which commit?
alex: Landed 1746500000, canary -> full rollout by 1746539000. The selector now biases toward micro-kernels for short sequences.
sam: Do we have syscall counters? I suspect more small grpc write/syscall traffic.
perf-bot: CPU profile uploaded: https://perf.redwood/trace/abc123 (sampled flamegraph).
dave: I pulled the profile — the hot path is lots of tiny memcpy + writev overhead. Also see repeated kv cache evict calls interleaved.
jin: Theory: smaller kernel reduces per-kernel compute but increases fragmentation on host frames, more small-stream fragments -> more parse/assemble cycles -> kv cache churn (prefix miss + evict).
maria: That matches telemetry: kv hit-rate dipped ~6% at the same window. We should consider coalescing host writes and tweak batching heuristics.
alex: Quick repro patch idea: add a micro-coalesce window on the host egress of 0.5ms to aggregate small frames; also gate kernel selection to prefer same-kernel grouping when multiple requests share seq-length +/- 8 tokens.
sam: micro-coalesce sounds low risk. Coalesce implementation (very small snippet):
```
// host/egress/coalesce.cc
if (queue.peek_total_size() < 2048 && age < 500us) 
  coalesce_and_write();
else
  flush();
```

dave: Also tune kvcache soft_limit to avoid thrash. bump soft_limit -> 0.8 and make eviction quantum larger so we don't evict tiny amounts repeatedly.
jin: +1. On batching heuristics: prefer grouping by kernel fingerprint and seq_len_bucket so kernel hop is reduced. Example: seq_len_bucket = floor(len/16).
maria: Proposed canary plan: 1) enable egress coalesce + kernel-grouping on a single canary pool 2) bump kv soft_limit on the same pool 3) run synthetic workload (same mix as user traffic) and monitor p50/p95, kv hit-rate, syscall rate.
alex: I'll run microbench now. Running the 1.2M token test with and without coalesce+kv tweaks.
perf-bot: Run queued: run-1746543300.

-- 15m later --

alex: Results: baseline -> coalesce+kv tweak
- p50 decode: 34ms -> 32ms (-6%)
- p95 decode: 190ms -> 156ms (-18%)
- kv hit-rate: 88.6% -> 92.1%
- grpc small-write syscalls/sec: 8.6k -> 2.1k

dave: That looks promising. Reduced syscall storm and improved kv locality.
maria: Any negative side effects on tail for very large sequences?
jin: I checked tail for >1024 tokens — unaffected; kernel-grouping keeps large seqs on the larger kernels.
sam: I opened a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6321 — includes coalesce, kernel-group heuristic + kv soft_limit config.
alex: PR 6321 notes: default coalesce window 500us, max coalesce bytes 2048, kernel-group bucket 16 tokens, kv.soft_limit 0.8, eviction_quantum 5%
dave: Let's roll in 5% increments, watch kv hit-rate and syscall metric. If anything regresses revert quickly.
maria: Agree. I'll create runbook: rollback if kv hit-rate drops >2% or p95 increases >10% over baseline.
alex: Plan to deploy to canary tonight at 22:00 UTC, I'll post results. :thumbsup:
jin: Thanks all — good catch.
perf-bot: Canary scheduled: 1746549000.
thread_text: Hosts-side coalesce + kv tweak to fix eviction thrash after kernel selector change
